title: Compact UI routes of the kernel: HTML fragment to native widgets (html-visual), screen archetypes (screen), whole page with bindings (html data)

capabilities.title: HTML/CSS fragment into an existing screen or block (native widgets)
capabilities.summary: The fragment becomes native widgets under an existing parent: div->Container, tags->IAdvancedHtml, text->Text, `{{ expr }}`->Expression (an OutSystems expression, never JavaScript), input/checkbox/textarea/select/button/a/label/img, `<div list as>`, `<div if>`/`<div else>`, `<Block name :Input @Event><slot>`; names must exist in the module; `<style>` is rewritten under the fragment root class. It is a translator of a closed table, not a general HTML/JS converter: logic, data and variables stay native.

depends.unless: the parent screen or block already exists (the fragment always needs an existing parent)

alternatives.when: a whole new page with a bindings manifest

capabilities.guidance: The widgets it creates are the ones of ui.widget, ui.input, ui.list, ui.dropdown and ui.block-instance: their evidence is stated there per role. Events: `onclick` names an existing action; `<Block @Event>` sets the instance Handler and passes the event parameters by name.

limits.text: Rejected: script, an <i> without weight, names that do not exist, tags outside the table, `#id` selectors, `@import`/at-statements, `<style media>`, attributes on an If or a block instance; logic, data and events stay in native verbs.
The parent must be inside an IMobileScreen or IMobileBlock; the fragment never creates logic, data or variables.

differences: IIcon has Weight on ODC (mandatory in the fragment)

limits.text: Rejected: script, names that do not exist, tags outside the table, `#id` selectors; logic, data and events stay in native verbs. Traditional Web screens are not a target of this op.

differences: IIcon has no Weight on O11

capabilities.title: Screen archetypes (cards, table, detail, form, dashboard) by op screen
capabilities.summary: One `screen` op declares screens by kind with source (entity or action), search, filters (native dropdown over a static entity), fields/columns/tabs/actions; the compiler composes OutSystemsUI blocks already referenced by the module (Search, Pagination, CardSectioned, Tabs, Gallery/Carousel, Counter).

alternatives.when: the screen needs anything outside the archetypes, or the ODC proofs are needed today (raw verbs are the proven path there)

capabilities.guidance: Deliver directly (the deliver call validates and refuses before any change; a headless proof only when the person asks for one); declare the required blocks by reading context.reads MobileBlockSignature.

limits.text: Accepted by the compiler for CrossDevice modules but no ODC job runs it (proven on O11: screen-spec-*.json). Form fields are input|textarea|checkbox only (no dropdown field); existing screen names are refused; the referenced OutSystemsUI blocks must exist in the module.
Only Reactive and Mobile screens are supported by the archetypes: a Traditional Web module is refused ('only Reactive and Mobile screens are supported'); an unknown kind is refused.

differences: proven in Reactive and Mobile (screen-spec-cards-mobile) modules

capabilities.title: Whole page from HTML + bindings manifest (op html data)
capabilities.summary: The page HTML/CSS plus a typed bindings manifest (text, field, list, visible, style, class, date, navigate, call, refresh, page, block) compiled to native widgets, data sources and screen actions; CSS installed in the theme author half.

alternatives.when: the logic stays native and only a fragment is authored (proven on both lanes)

capabilities.guidance: JavaScript only enters as declared scripts[] that become client actions with a JavaScript node (basic input types); the browser rendering of the result is not verified by the kernel.

limits.text:
No ODC job (proven on O11: html-dashboard-reactive.json). id selectors in CSS are always refused;
, ,
Only Reactive and Mobile screens: Traditional Web modules are refused by the html op. The legacy `data.components` (HtmlComponents, JavaScript parsed, never evaluated) is not the route to use.
